title: auth: trusted issuer cert auth (self-operated CA, CN as username)
description: Extend client cert auth to trust any cert signed by a configured issuer CA, not just individually pinned certs. This lets an operator run a tiny self-signed CA and issue per-user or per-device certs without updating the server config for each one. Config: [[auth.trusted_issuers]] with either cert = '/path/to/ca.crt' (PEM) or spki_sha256 = 'sha256:<hex>' (public key hash — survives CA cert renewal with same key). Username: the leaf cert CN field; must exist as a user in CredentialStore or be explicitly mapped. CN denylist optional for revocation without re-issuing the CA. Auth priority order on a TLS connection: (1) leaf fingerprint match (1c8.10), (2) issuer chain match, (3) Basic/Bearer. Implementation: rustls ClientCertVerifier receives the full peer cert chain; for issuer auth, parse the leaf cert with x509-parser, extract the TBS cert bytes, verify the CA signature using the issuer's public key. ~100 lines, no new deps if x509-parser is already in the tree. Generation workflow: openssl req -x509 -newkey ed25519 ... (CA); openssl req + openssl x509 -req -CA ... (leaf per user). Apply to same surfaces as 1c8.10: NNTPS, JMAP HTTPS, admin HTTP.
